title: 2025-04-30 Redwood POC weekly sync - ACME ML
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on cost/unit economics. Reviewed benchmark numbers for tokens/sec/$, caching benefits, and batching tradeoffs. Agreed on next benchmarks and data to share.
transcript:
Header: 2025-04-30 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45min | Attendees: Lena (AE), Marcus (SE) - Redwood; Priya, Daniel, Marta - ACME ML
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh small agenda today quick cost review the numbers Marcus ran and then figure out next steps for the dedicated bench. ok? 
[00:20] Priya: yep sounds good, we especially wanna understand tokens per dollar and whether caching will actually move the needle for our chat flows, which are fairly repeated prefixes.
[00:35] Marcus: cool — I'll share screen — so the headline: baseline hosted run on model-redwood-v1 cpu/rtx-ish, we measured about 600 tokens/sec median with no batching and no cache, cost roughly $0.12 per 1k tokens in our hosted profile, which maps to roughly 5k tokens/sec per dollar in our math here — it's a bit of a weird metric but it helps compare configs.
[01:02] Marta: sorry can you repeat the per-dollar figure? I got lost.
[01:05] Marcus: yeah so: tokens/sec per $1 — think of it as how much sustained throughput you get for a dollar of spend. baseline ~5,000 tokens/sec/$.
[01:20] Daniel: ok makes sense as a proxy.
[01:25] Priya: what about batching — you mentioned higher throughput?
[01:28] Marcus: right, with batching enabled (batch size 8) throughput jumped to ~1.6k tokens/sec median, that's about 14k tokens/sec/$, so almost 3x better unit economics. but caveat: p95 latency goes up from ~420ms to ~1.1s, so for low-latency interactive UX it's a tradeoff.
[02:00] Priya: that's a big p95 jump.
[02:03] Marcus: yeah and the pattern matters — when traffic is spiky small batches are less effective; continuous steady traffic gives biggest wins.
[02:18] Lena: also caching — Marcus you had results for prefix caching and KV hits?
[02:22] Marcus: yes, we simulated a typical support chat pattern with 35% repeated prefixes. prefix caching (response-level reuse and prefix KV) gave us ~28% reduction in tokens sent to the model; additional KV cache hit rate for conversation context hovered around 12-18% depending on TTL. net cost reduction in our run ~22% with conservative settings.
[02:48] Priya: so combined batching + caching is multiplicative? like would we see both gains?
[02:53] Marcus: mostly additive but there are interactions — batching reduces per-token overhead so caching savings become proportionally smaller but absolute cost still falls. in our combined run: batching + caching gave about 4x tokens/sec/$ vs baseline but p95 moved to ~1.2s. 
[03:15] Marta: for our product we need p50 under 300ms and p95 under 900ms ideally, so that 1.2s p95 is a problem.
[03:25] Daniel: can we tune batch size or target latency SLOs in the runtime to keep p95 lower?
[03:29] Marcus: yes, you can cap batch delay and max batch size; example: batch size 4 with max waiting time 40ms gave us 2x throughput improvement and p95 at ~680ms. so it's a middle ground.
[03:50] Priya: that sounds promising. what's the recommended config for interactive chat with some async fallback?
[03:55] Lena: typical approach: primary route with batch cap 4 and 40ms max delay, fallback to single-request low-latency route if latency constrained or for priority users. that's what we propose for pilot.
[04:12] Priya: and Dedicated capacity — how different are the economics?
[04:15] Marcus: dedicated GPUs reduce variability and give better throughput; in our tests using Dedicated (1 reserved rig equivalent) we saw a steady 2x improvement vs hosted baseline for same model and config, so roughly 10k tokens/sec/$ (after amortizing reserved costs) depending on commit size. big caveat is committed monthly cost vs burst flexibility.
[04:40] Marta: can you put numbers with committed monthly pricing? our finance needs that to compare.
[04:44] Marcus: yes we'll model that — rough example: with a 1 unit dedicated commit we estimate amortized infra cost ~ $6k/month which for your steady 24/7 traffic maps to X tokens per dollar — we'll share the spreadsheet with exact math.
[05:00] Lina: (voice) sorry wrong line —
[05:02] Lena: haha no worries.
[05:05] Priya: any impact from quantization on latency and cost?
[05:08] Marcus: quantization reduces memory and often improves throughput; in local bench q4_0 gave similar quality for your workloads and ~15% throughput improvement. accuracy regressions were minor on our test prompts but we need more eval sets from you.
[05:28] Daniel: about caching TTLs — what's recommended safety for secure contexts? we're worried about PII and user messages.
[05:35] Marcus: state can be cached client-side or server-side with encryption; TTL depends on retention policy — we recommend per-conversation ephemeral TTL of 1h for KV when messages are non-sensitive and zero for PII. Also keys can be KMS-protected. we can map to your compliance requirements.
[05:58] Priya: ok. any sign of hallucination or quality change with batching or caching?
[06:02] Marcus: caching doesn't change generation quality inherently; batching can affect temperature scheduling if not handled correctly but our runtime normalizes request-level sampling. we didn't see measurable regen quality diffs in quick tests.
[06:20] Marta: what about production monitoring — how will we see cost by route and by token?
[06:25] Lena: Redwood console gives token-level cost breakdowns per route and model, and you can export per-token logs; we'll enable higher retention for the pilot and ship the dashboard views.
[06:40] Priya: perfect. next steps?
[06:42] Lena: summary: Marcus to run dedicated capacity bench with batch cap scenarios and KV enabled; Priya to share 7-day token distribution trace; Lena to circulate updated cost spreadsheet. we'll aim to reconvene after we have the 24h dedicated bench results.
[07:00] Marta: timeline wise can we get those in one week? our internal deadline is 2025-05-12.
[07:06] Lena: yes we can hit it — we'll try to get bench by 2025-05-07 and spreadsheet by 2025-05-02.
[07:12] Daniel: ok will share traces by Friday.
[07:15] Priya: thanks all.
[07:17] Lena: thanks everyone, ending now.

Notes: transcription had occasional label errors; phone feedback at 5:00
References shared: https://redwood.ai/sheets/poc-acme-costs (benchmark spreadsheet), security packet link: https://redwood.ai/security/poc-acme

Marcus Chen - run dedicated-capacity bench (batch size 4/8, max wait 40ms/100ms, KV enabled) and upload logs by 2025-05-07
Priya Desai - provide 7-day traffic/token distribution and sample prompt set (anonymized) by 2025-05-02
Daniel Park - confirm compliance constraints for caching/TTL and share redacted examples by 2025-05-02

ACME to send 7-day token distribution and sample prompts (due 2025-05-02)
